clue.text: Left-wing alliance meeting in promenade

parts.note: something in is fashionable or well liked, that is, popular
a seaside promenade is the front, as in the seafront

explanation.surface: A coalition of left-wingers gathers on a seaside walkway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' is a link word joining the two pieces side by side; 'in' is not a container signal but the adjective meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular front is a coalition of left-wing and centrist parties, such as those formed in 1930s France and Spain.

clue.text: Leading seaman's sketch of sole

indicators.note: the sketch comes first, leading the sailor, so it stands in front in the answer

parts.note: a sketch or outline drawing is a plan
a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A senior naval rating draws a fish, a sole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading seaman' looks like the naval rank; split it so 'Leading' tells you the sketch goes before the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The anatomical adjective plantar describes the underside of the foot, its sole.

clue.text: Food manufacture

definitions.meaning: farm crops such as fruit and vegetables sold as food
to make or turn out goods

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means fresh farm food; as a verb it means to make or manufacture.

clue.text: Left to love and lust outrageously in this bed of roses

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: behaving outrageously means acting wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone abandons themselves to love and lust in a life of luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'in this' are link words; L, O, AND and LUST are mixed up by 'outrageously'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotus land is an idyllic place of ease and indulgence, which is what a bed of roses means.

clue.text: Channels for sporting events

definitions.meaning: a race is a strong current or a channel carrying water, as in a mill race
contests of speed such as horse or running competitions

explanation.definitionFit: A mill race is a water channel, and races are also contests of speed.

clue.text: Platform prepared for the beak

definitions.meaning: a raised stand for a speaker or conductor
in zoology the beak or snout of an animal has a Latin-derived name

explanation.surface: A stage is set up for the magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beak' is British slang for a magistrate, which makes the surface about a courtroom dais; in fact it is the zoological sense, a bird's or insect's bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word means a speaker's raised platform and, in biology, a beak-like snout.

clue.text: Material witness provided by Granny Sharp

parts.note: nan is a familiar name for a grandmother
a keen blade is a sharp one

explanation.surface: A key witness in a case is supplied by an old lady called Granny Sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material witness' is a legal phrase, but only 'Material' is the definition; 'witness provided by' merely links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth, originally made in Nanjing, so it is a fabric or material.

clue.text: Shrink on seeing circus performer

definitions.meaning: a circus act who does stunts on a bicycle or unicycle

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist reacts on watching a clown pedal past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trick cyclist' is British rhyming-style slang for a psychiatrist, playing on 'psychiatrist'; literally it is a stunt rider in a circus.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is jocular slang for a psychiatrist and literally names a stunt bicycle rider.

clue.text: Expel from a party in true fashion

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it anew, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone is thrown out of a political party in proper style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and 'in' are link words; A, DO and TRUE are shuffled by 'fashion', which looks like a noun but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be read out of a group or party is to be formally expelled from it.

clue.text: When in island makes tour of betting places

indicators.note: the island goes all round the other words, touring them, so it surrounds them

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers on an island take a trip round its gambling venues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'island' here is Cos, also spelt Kos, in the Dodecanese; 'When' is a sense of 'as' easily overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Casinos are establishments where people gamble, so they are places for betting.

clue.text: Egghead's associate makes decisive moves on board

parts.note: an egghead is an intellectual or scholar, here in the possessive
a mate is a companion or associate

explanation.surface: An academic's colleague takes charge of a board meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link word. The board is a chessboard: this is the four-move checkmate that catches beginners.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholar's mate is a quick chess checkmate in four moves, decisive play on the board.

clue.text: Copper takes racketeers' pictures

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
ticket touts are racketeers who resell tickets at inflated prices

explanation.surface: A police officer seizes the photographs of a gang of criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the element; 'takes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut-outs are pictures or shapes cut from paper or card.

clue.text: Rum sort of yell

definitions.meaning: a kind of rum, the cheap dark spirit of Newfoundland

explanation.surface: A strange kind of shout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the British adjective meaning odd, but it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a Newfoundland rum and also a harsh shrill cry or yell.

clue.text: Priest touring see with crook

indicators.note: the priest goes round the other letter, touring it

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest
v stands for vide, Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: A clergyman travels round a diocese with a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a bishop's diocese and 'crook' like a criminal, but see is V and the crook is a bend.
explanation.definitionFit: A crook is a bend or hook, as in the crook of an arm, which is a curve.

clue.text: With belly in unusually bad order, lain over

indicators.note: unusually signals that these letters come out in an unusual arrangement

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

indicators.note: over here means knocked over, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lies down with a sore stomach in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. ABD (from 'bad', 'unusually') + OM + INAL (from 'lain', 'over').
explanation.definitionFit: Abdominal is the adjective for the abdomen, the belly, so it means concerning the belly.

clue.text: Cleaner faces ruin, hooked on dope and heroin

indicators.note: the following pieces are attached after the first one, hooked on to it

parts.note: to dish someone's hopes is to ruin them
a dope or clot is a fool
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady is ruined by drug addiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faces' and 'and' are link words; 'hooked on' and 'dope' suggest drugs, but dope is a fool, CLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishcloth is used to wash dishes, so it is a cleaning cloth, a cleaner.

clue.text: Soldiers given order thus to retreat

parts.note: a command is an order

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: so means thus, as in 'and so it happened'

explanation.surface: Troops are told to fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link word; 'to retreat' turns SO into OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Commandos are soldiers trained for raids, so the plural matches the definition.

clue.text: Warlike skill shown when wearing coat of mail, perhaps

indicators.note: the skill is wrapped in the other letters as in a coat worn round it
perhaps signals the letters may be in some other order

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of fencing

explanation.surface: A knight shows his warlike ability while dressed in chain mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown when' are link words; MIAL, from 'mail' with 'perhaps', goes round ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial means relating to war, so it is a synonym of warlike.

clue.text: Not for touching

definitions.meaning: opposed, in opposition to a proposal
in contact with, as a ladder leaning on a wall

explanation.definitionFit: The word means opposed to (not for) and also in contact with, leaning on something.

clue.text: Tree many be deal? Right?

indicators.note: a slip for 'may be': the letters may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A tree might be timber, mightn't it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'many be' is a misprint for 'may be', signalling an anagram of DEAL; 'deal' looks like timber (deal is pine wood) but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family that grows by water.

clue.text: Ham sandwich consumed with a drink standing

indicators.note: the drink is two slices round the filling, like a sandwich
in a down clue, standing means set upright, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A ham sandwich eaten with a drink at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham sandwich' looks like lunch; 'Ham' is the definition and 'sandwich' the container. 'standing' reads the drink upwards, as suits a down clue; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is an inexpert performer or a radio hobbyist, someone unpaid and unskilled.

clue.text: Seed with thick centre about to burst open

indicators.note: about means around, here turning the letters round into a new order
the centre of a word is its letters minus the first and last

explanation.surface: A seed with a dense core is ready to split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes HIC from 'thick'; with SEED these letters are mixed by 'about'. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dehisce is a botanical verb for a seed pod or fruit splitting open to release its contents.

clue.text: Intrusive moves made by voguish explorer, say

parts.note: in means fashionable or voguish

indicators.note: say means spoken, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Cecil Rhodes, the British colonialist who opened up southern Africa

explanation.surface: A trendy adventurer makes forceful advances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are incursions or advances into territory, intrusive moves.

clue.text: Cloth that sounds swell

indicators.note: these words say the answer is heard like another word

parts.note: a surge is a swell, as of the sea

explanation.surface: A fabric that has a fine noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' looks like the old adjective meaning excellent; it is the noun, a rising wave.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a hard-wearing twilled woollen cloth used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: Leading 19 down — talk of the town

indicators.note: the talk is placed in front, leading the other piece

parts.note: chat is informal talk
the answer to 19 down is defined there by its synonym ham

explanation.surface: Gossip about the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the' are link words. Chatham is a town in Kent with a historic naval dockyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatham is a dockyard town in Kent, in south-east England.

clue.text: Bar in to the right is less crowded

indicators.note: the bar is put into the following words

parts.note: taken as written
an inn is a pub or bar

explanation.surface: A pub on the right-hand side has fewer customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word; 'to the right' looks like a direction but supplies letters, with the pub put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A thinner crowd is a sparser one, with fewer people in it.

clue.text: Disturbed by short section in the OT

indicators.note: the section is put inside the other letters

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament
a verse is a short numbered section of a chapter of scripture

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by a brief passage of the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'the' are link words; 'short section' looks like a clipping signal but is a verse, a short section of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Overset is an old word for upset, so it means disturbed or overturned.

clue.text: Dandy outfit buck's put on

parts.note: an outfit is a set of clothes
a buck is a gymnastic vaulting horse

explanation.surface: A dandy's fashionable outfit is worn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' are link words saying the clothes go on the horse. A gym buck is a short vaulting horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse is a person who loves wearing fashionable clothes, much like a dandy.
